module_title: Learning Outcomes, Authentic Assessment & Constructivist Alignment
introduction: This intermediate tier transitions to the actual mechanics of implementing CBE in a classroom. It differentiates between Learning Objectives and Learning Outcomes, and details the specific types of assessments required to measure true competency.

core_concepts.title: Learning Objectives vs. Learning Outcomes (LOs)
core_concepts.description:
Examiners frequently test this distinction:
- Learning Objectives: Teacher-centric. What the teacher intends to cover in the lesson. (e.g., 'I will teach the process of photosynthesis').
- Learning Outcomes (LOs): Student-centric and measurable. What the student will explicitly be able to do by the end of the lesson. (e.g., 'The student will be able to draw and explain the water cycle using correct scientific vocabulary'). CBE is entirely driven by LOs.

core_concepts.title: Authentic Assessment (Performance Assessment)
core_concepts.description:
You cannot test a competency with a standard multiple-choice question (MCQ) alone. 
- CBE requires Authentic Assessment: Testing students in real-world or simulated environments. 
- Example: If the competency is 'Public Speaking', a written test on speech rules is useless. The authentic assessment is having the student deliver a 3-minute speech to a live audience.

core_concepts.title: Rubrics in CBE
core_concepts.description:
Because CBE evaluates complex skills rather than simple right/wrong answers, teachers must use **Rubrics**.
- A rubric is a transparent scoring guide used to evaluate performance, a product, or a project. It breaks down the competency into distinct criteria and describes what 'Mastery', 'Developing', and 'Beginning' look like for each criterion.

core_concepts.title: Formative Assessment as the Backbone of CBE
core_concepts.description: In a competency-based system, Summative assessment (final exams) takes a backseat. Formative assessment (continuous, ongoing evaluation during the learning process) is the primary tool. It provides immediate feedback, allowing the student to try again, correct mistakes, and eventually reach mastery.

important_entities.name: SMART Criteria for Learning Outcomes
important_entities.key_fact: How to write effective CBE outcomes.
important_entities.significance: A Learning Outcome must be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. Vague terms like 'The student will understand...' or 'The student will know...' are banned in CBE because 'understanding' cannot be objectively measured. Instead, use action verbs like 'define', 'calculate', 'construct', or 'critique'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: CBE strictly prohibits Norm-Referenced Assessment (comparing students against each other, ranking them 1st, 2nd, 3rd). CBE exclusively uses **Criterion-Referenced Assessment** (comparing the student ONLY against the competency standard). In CBE, theoretically, every single student in the class can score 100% if they master the skill.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use this anchor: Objectives are what the school puts IN. Outcomes are what the student puts OUT.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks 'Which type of assessment is most heavily relied upon in a Competency-Based Education framework?', choose **Formative Assessment** or **Criterion-Referenced Assessment**.
